Let \(g=A_5x\). For block \((i,i+1)\), the local Hessian is
\[
H=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
H^{-1}=\frac13\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Thus the energy decrease from updating block \(i\) is
\[
\frac12(g_i,g_{i+1})H^{-1}(g_i,g_{i+1})^T
=\frac13(g_i^2+g_ig_{i+1}+g_{i+1}^2).
\]
Since \(f_5(x)=\frac12x^TA_5x=\frac12g^TA_5^{-1}g\), if
\[
\mu(p):=\inf_{g\ne0}
\frac{\frac23\sum_{i=1}^4p_i(g_i^2+g_ig_{i+1}+g_{i+1}^2)}
{g^TA_5^{-1}g},
\]
then
\[
\Gamma(p)=1-\mu(p).
\]

Now take
\[
g_*=(2,1,2,1,2)^T.
\]
Solving \(A_5x=g_*\) gives
\[
x_*=(4,6,7,6,4)^T,
\]
and
\[
g_*^TA_5^{-1}g_*=g_*^Tx_*=42.
\]
Also every adjacent pair of \(g_*\) is either \((2,1)\) or \((1,2)\), so
\[
\frac23(g_i^2+g_ig_{i+1}+g_{i+1}^2)=\frac{14}{3}
\]
for all \(i\). Hence for every probability vector \(p\),
\[
\mu(p)\le \frac{14/3}{42}=\frac19.
\]
So \(\Gamma(p)\ge 8/9\).

Equality requires \(g_*\) to be an eigenvector for the generalized minimum, i.e.
\[
D_pg_*=\frac19A_5^{-1}g_*=\frac19(4,6,7,6,4)^T,
\]
where \(D_p\) is the quadratic-form matrix of the expected decrease. Componentwise this gives
\[
\frac{5p_1}{3}=\frac49,\quad
\frac{4(p_1+p_2)}3=\frac69,\quad
\frac{5(p_2+p_3)}3=\frac79,\quad
\frac{4(p_3+p_4)}3=\frac69,\quad
\frac{5p_4}{3}=\frac49.
\]
Thus uniquely
\[
p_*=\left(\frac4{15},\frac7{30},\frac7{30},\frac4{15}\right).
\]

For this \(p_*\), the smallest generalized eigenvalue is indeed \(1/9\). On the reflection-even subspace it has eigenvector \(g_*\); on the reflection-odd subspace the eigenvalues are \(4/15\) and \(26/45\), both larger than \(1/9\). The even characteristic polynomial factors as
\[
-\left(\lambda-\frac19\right)
\left(27\lambda^2-\frac{141}{5}\lambda+\frac{168}{25}\right),
\]
so the \(1/9\)-eigenspace is one-dimensional. Therefore the worst-case initial vectors are exactly the nonzero multiples of
\[
v_*=(4,6,7,6,4).
\]

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{
\left(
\left(\frac4{15},\frac7{30},\frac7{30},\frac4{15}\right),
\frac89,
(4,6,7,6,4)
\right)
}.
\]
